notes: Each program's facts come from its own page (or a state agency page). Every quote is re-checked against the live page on each sync; a program whose quote disappears is skipped and reported, never shown stale.
Before approving: open each source URL, confirm the summary says nothing the quotes don't, and confirm 'paid' is true only where a quote says participants are paid.
FareStart and Year Up United describe their training as free/tuition-free; neither page says participants are paid, so 'paid' is null for both.
Path Forward is national; it is marked statewide so it can match anyone returning after a career break.
Set status to 'reviewed' and fill reviewed_by / reviewed_on to load these programs.

programs.name: FareStart Job Training
programs.summary: Free job training in food-based businesses, with case management and help with basic needs, for people overcoming poverty, homelessness, substance use disorder, incarceration, or other barriers to employment.
quotes: FareStart’s free job training programs skill, reskill and upskill students so they are prepared for the career pathways of their choosing.
If you are overcoming poverty, homelessness, substance use disorder, incarceration or other barriers to employment, we can help.

programs.name: Year Up United (Seattle)
programs.summary: Tuition-free job training for young adults aged 18-29, with hands-on experience and job placement support.

source.name: Year Up United: Job Training in Seattle, WA

quotes: Designed for young adults aged 18-29, our flexible programs offer training through virtual and in-person engagements to equip you with the skills needed for full-time employment.
With tuition-free opportunities, you'll gain hands-on experience and professional development

programs.name: Pioneer Human Services reentry training and employment
programs.summary: Reentry services across Washington for people transitioning from prison and jail, including job-readiness training (G.R.O.W. in Spokane) and an entrepreneurship program (INVEST in South Seattle).
quotes: we provide comprehensive reentry services in Washington state for individuals transitioning from prison and jail

Training options include the Guiding Reentry Opportunities for Workforce Development (G.R.O.W.) job-readiness training program in Spokane and the Incarceration to New Ventures: Elevating Success Together (INVEST) entrepreneurship program in South Seattle

programs.name: Path Forward returnship directory
programs.summary: A national directory and Returnship Matcher for people returning to work after a career break, including parents and other caregivers.
quotes: We provide resources specifically for people returning to work after a career break.
The programs overcome the hiring stigma that makes returning to work a tough road for parents and other caregivers.

programs.name: WorkFirst Community Jobs and Career Jump
programs.organization: Washington State Department of Social and Health Services (WorkFirst)
programs.summary: Paid work experience for WorkFirst participants; Career Jump places participants with an employer that has agreed to hire them at the end, above minimum wage.

source.name: WorkFirst Handbook 8.3: Community Jobs
source.authority: Washington State Department of Social and Health Services

quotes: Career Jump is a subset of Community Jobs, which offers participants an opportunity to gain paid work experience with an employer that has agreed to hire them at the end of their program.
the employment opportunity will be compensated above minimum wage
